books.title: Lecture 1: Pelvic skeleton, joints and organization of pelvic viscera
books.author: Prof. Dr. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the bony pelvis, its joints and ligaments, inlet/outlet, and the arrangement of pelvic viscera and peritoneal pouches in males and females.

books.title: Lecture 2: Pelvic walls and pelvic floor
books.author: Prof. Dr. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the walls of the pelvis (anterior, posterior, lateral), piriformis, obturator internus, obturator fascia, and the pelvic floor (levator ani and coccygeus) with nerve supply, actions and clinical notes.

books.title: Lecture 3: Internal iliac vessels and sacral plexus
books.author: Prof. Dr. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the internal iliac artery and its anterior and posterior divisions and branches, internal iliac vein tributaries, median sacral artery, and the sacral plexus (formation and branches).

books.title: Lecture 4: Female reproductive system I (uterus)
books.author: Prof. Dr. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the female reproductive system I: the uterus (parts, cervix, position, relations, peritoneal covering), ligaments of the cervix and uterus, broad ligament, factors keeping the uterus in position, uterine prolapse, blood supply and lymphatic drainage.

books.title: Lecture 5: Female reproductive system II (ovary, tubes, vagina, external genitalia)
books.author: Prof. Dr. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the female reproductive system II: the ovary (site, fossa, surfaces, ligaments, blood supply, drainage), uterine tubes, vagina (relations, fornices, supports, supply), external genitalia and greater vestibular glands.

books.title: Lecture 6: Female mammary gland (breast)
books.author: Prof. Dr. Maha Diaa Safwat
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the female mammary gland (breast): definition, shape, base, structure, blood supply, lymphatic drainage, clinical notes (breast cancer signs, abscess, gynecomastia), development from the milk ridge and congenital abnormalities.

books.title: Lecture 7: Male reproductive system
books.author: Prof. Dr. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the male reproductive system: testis, epididymis, scrotum, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, ejaculatory ducts, prostate, bulbourethral glands and penis, with blood supply, lymphatics and clinical notes (varicocele, benign prostatic hypertrophy).

books.title: Lecture 8: Perineum I
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the perineum I: boundaries and divisions, urogenital triangle, fascial layers, superficial and deep perineal pouches (boundaries and contents in males and females), and the perineal membrane with the structures piercing it.

books.title: Lecture 9: Perineum II
books.author: Prof. Wafaa Abdel Rahman
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the perineum II: the recto-anal triangle, ischiorectal fossa, pudendal canal, pudendal nerve, internal pudendal artery and the perineal body with its clinical importance.

books.title: Lecture 10: Kidney and ureter
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the kidney and ureter: site, size, shape, coverings, internal structure, hilum, anterior and posterior relations, blood supply and segments, lymphatics; ureter parts, constrictions, relations, supply; applied anatomy (ureteric stones, renal colic).

chunks.title: Overview: pelvic skeleton and hip bone
chunks.summary: Title slide (Prof. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany, Alexandria University). The pelvis is formed by two hip bones plus the sacrum posteriorly. Each hip bone is formed of three bones (ilium, ischium, pubis) that join at the acetabulum.

chunks.title: Iliac bone (ilium)
chunks.summary: Upper part of the hip bone. Iliac crest ends at the anterior superior and posterior superior iliac spines; anterior inferior and posterior inferior iliac spines lie below them. Pelvic (inner) surface with the iliac fossa; gluteal (outer) surface giving origin to gluteal muscles; auricular surface articulating with the sacrum; iliac tuberosity behind it.

chunks.title: Pubic bone and ischial bone
chunks.summary: Pubic bone (anterior part of hip bone): body articulating at the symphysis pubis with pubic tubercle and pubic crest (medial to tubercle); superior pubic ramus with pectineal line and pectineal surface; inferior pubic ramus joining the ischial ramus to form the ischiopubic ramus. Ischial bone (lower part): ramus, ischiopubic ramus (pubic arch is formed by the ischiopubic rami of both sides), ischial tuberosity, ischial spine separating greater sciatic notch (above) from lesser sciatic notch (below).

chunks.title: Sacrum: shape and surfaces
chunks.summary: Triangular bone forming the posterior bone of the pelvic skeleton; apex below, base above; formed of 5 fused sacral vertebrae; base has the sacral promontory and an ala on each side; 4 surfaces. Anterior surface: concave, 4 pairs of anterior sacral foramina, 4 transverse ridges (lines of fusion), origin of piriformis. Lateral surface: auricular surface in front and sacral tuberosity behind (auricular surface forms the sacroiliac joint). Posterior surface: convex, median sacral crest, 4 pairs of posterior sacral foramina, sacral hiatus, upper opening of the canal; sacral cornua articulate with coccygeal cornua.

chunks.title: Sacral canal, sacral hiatus and coccyx
chunks.summary: Sacral canal is the lower part of the vertebral canal; upper opening on the dorsum of the first sacral piece, lower opening is the sacral hiatus. Contents: dura mater and arachnoid, lateral sacral arteries, 5 pairs of sacral nerves, 1 pair of coccygeal nerves, filum terminale (lower extension of pia mater). Structures exiting the sacral hiatus: 5th sacral nerves, coccygeal nerves, filum terminale. Coccyx: 2-4 fused coccygeal vertebrae.

chunks.title: Pelvic joints and ligaments
chunks.summary: Symphysis pubis: joint between the bodies of the pubic bones with an intervening disc; a secondary cartilaginous joint. Sacroiliac joint has 2 compartments: anterior part between the auricular surfaces (synovial plane joint, sliding movements) and posterior part between the tuberosities (fibrous joint, syndesmosis, limited mobility); ligaments: anterior, interosseous and posterior sacroiliac. Sacrotuberous ligament (sacrum and coccyx to ischial tuberosity) and sacrospinous ligament (to ischial spine) convert the greater and lesser sciatic notches into foramina.

chunks.title: Pelvic inlet, outlet, divisions and position
chunks.summary: Pelvic inlet: bounded by symphysis pubis, pubic crest, pubic tubercle, pectineal line, arcuate line and ala of sacrum on each side, and the sacral promontory posteriorly. Pelvic outlet: inferior surface of symphysis pubis, pubic arch, ischial tuberosities, sacrotuberous ligaments and tip of coccyx. Greater (false) pelvis lies above the inlet and contains abdominal viscera; lesser (true) pelvis lies between inlet and outlet and contains pelvic viscera and perineum. Anatomical position: pubic tubercles and anterior superior iliac spines lie in the same vertical plane.

chunks.title: Pelvic viscera and peritoneal reflections (male and female)
chunks.summary: Males: bladder most anterior with urethra from its lower end, prostate below the bladder, rectum most posterior; peritoneum passes from the anterior abdominal wall to the bladder's upper surface and upper posterior surface, then onto the rectum forming the rectovesical pouch. Females: bladder anterior, uterus above the bladder with the cervix behind it, vagina behind the bladder, rectum posterior, uterine tube on each side opening into the uterus and ending at the ovary; peritoneum passes from the abdominal wall to the bladder then the lower uterus forming the uterovesical pouch, then covers the uterus and posterior vagina and reflects onto the rectum forming the rectovaginal (rectouterine) pouch of Douglas.

chunks.title: Self-test: true/false and MCQ with answers
chunks.summary: End-of-lecture questions with answers. True/false: lesser pelvis lies above the pelvic inlet (False); rectovesical pouch is a peritoneal pouch in females (False); 4th and 5th pairs of sacral nerves exit the sacral hiatus (False); symphysis pubis is a secondary cartilaginous joint (True). MCQ: type of the anterior part of the sacroiliac joint (synovial plane). Final slide is a thank-you slide.

chunks.title: Pelvic walls: anterior, posterior and lateral
chunks.summary: Title slide (Prof. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany). Anterior wall: pubic bones and symphysis pubis (antero-inferior wall in anatomical position). Posterior wall: sacrum and coccyx with piriformis muscles and the sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments (greater and lesser sciatic foramina). Lateral wall: obturator internus muscle and obturator fascia; obturator membrane closes the obturator foramen leaving the obturator canal; its inner aspect is covered by obturator internus and obturator fascia.

chunks.title: Piriformis, obturator internus and obturator fascia
chunks.summary: Piriformis: origin anterior surface of the middle 3 pieces of the sacrum; passes through the greater sciatic foramen to insert on the greater trochanter of the femur; nerve supply sacral plexus (S1,2); lateral rotation of thigh. Obturator internus: origin inner side of obturator membrane and bone around the obturator foramen; passes through the lesser sciatic foramen to the greater trochanter; nerve to obturator internus; lateral rotation of thigh. Obturator fascia covers the inner surface of obturator internus and is thickened as the tendinous arch, which gives origin to levator ani.

chunks.title: Pelvic floor and levator ani: origin and puborectalis
chunks.summary: Pelvic floor separates the pelvic cavity above from the perineum below and slopes inferiorly and medially; formed of levator ani (anterior part) and coccygeus (posterior part) muscles of both sides. Levator ani origin: body of the pubic bone, tendinous arch (linear thickening of the obturator fascia) and ischial spine; divided into 3 parts, listed on the slide as puborectalis, pubococcygeus and ischiococcygeus (the next slides describe iliococcygeus). Puborectalis forms a U-shaped sling with its opposite side around the anorectal junction.

chunks.title: Pubococcygeus, iliococcygeus and levator ani diagrams
chunks.summary: Pubococcygeus attaches to the fibres of the opposite side in the midline around the urethra and vagina (pubovaginalis) in females, or around the urethra below the prostate (puboprostaticus) in males, and to the perineal body, anal sphincters, anococcygeal body and coccyx. Iliococcygeus attaches to the anococcygeal body and tip of the coccyx. Diagram pages show the pelvic diaphragm from below/above: urogenital (urethral) hiatus, vaginal canal, rectal hiatus, perineal body, pre-rectal fibres of puborectalis, anococcygeal ligament/body.

chunks.title: Levator ani nerve supply, actions, clinical notes; coccygeus
chunks.summary: Levator ani nerve supply S2,3,4. Actions: supports pelvic viscera (during forced acts); puborectalis maintains the anorectal angle so it must relax during defecation; acts as a sphincter of the vagina in females; reinforces the anal sphincters. Clinical notes: during labour the perineal body may be torn and levator ani affected, causing weakness of the pelvic floor and loss of support of pelvic viscera, which may lead to prolapse of the uterus. Coccygeus: posterior part of the pelvic floor, represents the inner side of the sacrospinous ligament; origin ischial spine; insertion last 2 pieces of the sacrum and first piece of the coccyx.

chunks.title: Self-test: true/false and MCQ with answers
chunks.summary: True/false: obturator internus passes through the greater sciatic foramen (False, it uses the lesser); coccygeus forms the posterior part of the pelvic floor (True); obturator fascia gives origin to obturator internus (False); tear of the perineal body may lead to prolapse of the uterus (True). MCQ: the muscle representing the inner side of the sacrospinous ligament is coccygeus. Ends with the thank-you slide.

chunks.title: Internal iliac artery: origin, course and divisions
chunks.summary: Title slide and diagrams of the abdominal aorta, common iliac artery, and internal and external iliac arteries. Internal iliac artery: the smaller of the 2 terminal branches of the common iliac artery; begins at the level of the lumbosacral angle; ends by dividing into anterior and posterior divisions near the upper border of the greater sciatic foramen.

chunks.title: Branches of the posterior division of the internal iliac artery
chunks.summary: Posterior division gives 3 branches: 1) ilio-lumbar artery, 2) two lateral sacral arteries, 3) superior gluteal artery. Diagrams show the posterior and anterior divisions and their branches in relation to the pelvic wall.

chunks.title: Anterior division: parietal branches
chunks.summary: Branches of the anterior division are parietal and visceral. Parietal branches: obturator artery, inferior gluteal artery, internal pudendal artery (diagrams show their course towards the pudendal canal and the ischial spine).

chunks.title: Anterior division: visceral branches and summary diagram
chunks.summary: Visceral branches: umbilical artery and its superior vesical branch (the occluded part forms the medial umbilical ligament); inferior vesical artery in the male (replaced by the vaginal artery in the female); uterine artery in the female; middle rectal artery. Summary diagram labels internal iliac, obturator, superior vesical, inferior vesical, lateral sacral, superior gluteal, inferior gluteal, internal pudendal and middle rectal arteries.

chunks.title: Internal iliac vein and median sacral artery
chunks.summary: Internal iliac vein: formed at the upper border of the greater sciatic notch; joins the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein. Tributaries: obturator, lateral sacral, internal pudendal, superior gluteal, inferior gluteal, vesical (from the vesical venous plexus), uterine (uterine venous plexus), vaginal (vaginal venous plexus) and middle rectal veins. Median sacral artery: arises at the termination of the abdominal aorta at L4; passes in front of L5, sacrum and coccyx; ends in front of the coccyx as the glomus coccygeum; branches: 5th pair of lumbar arteries, sacral branches, rectal branches.

chunks.title: Sacral plexus: formation, site and diagrams
chunks.summary: Sacral plexus formed by the ventral rami of L4, L5 and S1,2,3,4. L4 and L5 join to form the lumbosacral trunk, which joins the sacral plexus. Site: in front of the piriformis muscle. Diagrams show the plexus with the sympathetic trunk, gray rami communicantes, pelvic splanchnic nerves, and its branches (superior and inferior gluteal, nerve to obturator internus, nerve to quadratus femoris, sciatic with tibial and common peroneal parts, pudendal, perforating cutaneous, posterior cutaneous nerve of thigh).
keywords: L4 L5 S1 S2 S3 S4

chunks.title: Branches of the sacral plexus
chunks.summary: A) Pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2,3,4): parasympathetic fibres to the pelvic viscera. B) Branches to pelvic muscles: nerve to piriformis. C) Branches to the lower limb (through the greater sciatic foramen to the gluteal region): sciatic nerve, superior gluteal nerve, inferior gluteal nerve, nerve to quadratus femoris, posterior cutaneous nerve of thigh, perforating cutaneous nerve. D) Branches to the perineum (greater sciatic foramen to the gluteal region then lesser sciatic foramen to the perineum): pudendal nerve and nerve to obturator internus. The sciatic and pudendal nerves are the 2 terminal branches of the sacral plexus.

chunks.title: Self-test: true/false and MCQ with answers
chunks.summary: True/false: 4th pair of lumbar arteries arises from the median sacral artery (False; the 5th pair does); inferior gluteal artery arises from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery (True); lumbosacral trunk is formed of L3 and L4 (False; L4 and L5); pudendal nerve is a terminal branch of the sacral plexus (True). MCQ: the branch of the posterior division of the internal iliac artery is the superior gluteal artery. Ends with the thank-you slide.

chunks.title: Female reproductive organs and parts of the uterus
chunks.summary: Title slide and overview diagram of the female reproductive organs. Parts of the female reproductive system: 1) uterus, 2) uterine tubes, 3) ovaries, 4) vagina, 5) external genital organs. Diagram of the parts of the uterus: fundus, cornua, body, cervix.

chunks.title: Uterus: site, parts, cervix and cervical canal
chunks.summary: Uterus lies in the pelvic cavity above the urinary bladder. Parts: fundus, body, and cervix (lower part, separated from the body by a constriction, the isthmus). The cervix lies partly outside and partly inside the vagina: supra-vaginal part and vaginal part. Cervical canal connects with the uterine cavity at the internal os and opens in the vagina at the external os; the external os is rounded in nulliparous women and a slit in women who have borne children.

chunks.title: Position of the uterus: anteverted and anteflexed
chunks.summary: Normal position is anteverted and anteflexed. Angle of version (anteversion, about 90 degrees) is between the cervix and the vagina (vagina and cervical canal). Angle of flexion (anteflexion, about 170 degrees) is between the body and the cervix (uterine and cervical canal). If the angle of flexion is more than 170 degrees the position is retroflexed; if the angle of version is more than 90 degrees it is retroverted.

chunks.title: Relations of the uterus and cervix
chunks.summary: Uterus relations: upper surface to small intestine and sigmoid colon; lower surface to urinary bladder with the utero-vesical pouch containing small intestine; laterally broad ligament and uterine artery. Supra-vaginal cervix: anteriorly base of the urinary bladder; posteriorly Douglas pouch containing small intestine and sigmoid colon; laterally broad ligament, uterine artery and ureter. Vaginal part of the cervix is surrounded by the vaginal fornices.

chunks.title: Peritoneal covering of the uterus
chunks.summary: Peritoneum is reflected from the upper surface of the urinary bladder at the isthmus to cover the lower surface of the body of the uterus, forming the utero-vesical pouch. It then covers the fundus and upper surface and continues down to cover the upper part of the posterior surface of the vagina, reflecting onto the rectum to form the recto-vaginal (Douglas) pouch. Laterally it extends from the uterine wall to the pelvic side wall as a double-layered fold, the broad ligament.

chunks.title: Ligaments supporting the cervix
chunks.summary: Ligaments supporting the cervix: anteriorly the pubocervical ligament; laterally the transverse cervical (cardinal, Mackenrodt's) ligament, the most important; posteriorly the uterosacral ligament. Diagram relates them to the bladder and rectum.

chunks.title: Ligaments of the uterus: round, ovarian and broad ligaments
chunks.summary: Diagrams of the ligaments of the uterus. Round ligament of the uterus runs from the cornua of the uterus to the labia majora. Ligament of the ovary (ovarian ligament) runs from the cornua of the uterus to the ovary. Broad ligament: a double-layered peritoneal fold from the lateral wall of the uterus to the side wall of the pelvis; anterior free border contains the uterine tube; posterior border on the pelvic floor; the ovary is attached to its superior surface by a peritoneal fold called the mesovarium.

chunks.title: Parts and contents of the broad ligament
chunks.summary: Parts of the broad ligament: mesometrium (between body of uterus, ovarian ligament and ovary), mesosalpinx (between uterine tube, ovarian ligament and ovary), suspensory ligament of the ovary (from the infundibulum of the uterine tube and ovary to the pelvic side wall, transmitting ovarian vessels and nerves) and mesovarium (connecting the ovary to the broad ligament). Contents: uterine tube, ovarian ligament, round ligament, ovarian artery, uterine artery, epoophoron and paroophoron.

chunks.title: Factors keeping the uterus in position; uterine prolapse
chunks.summary: Factors keeping the uterus in position: 1) ligaments (the most important, especially the cardinal ligament), 2) pelvic floor, 3) perineal body, 4) neighbouring organs. Clinical note, uterine prolapse: due to weakness of the supporting factors and injury of the pelvic floor; the uterus may descend with protrusion (telescoping) through the vagina.

chunks.title: Blood supply, venous and lymphatic drainage of the uterus
chunks.summary: Uterine artery: arises from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery; passes lateral to the cervix where it crosses the ureter; runs a tortuous course along the side of the uterus between the layers of the broad ligament to the uterine tube, where it turns laterally to anastomose with the ovarian artery; branches to the uterus, medial part of the uterine tube, vagina and ureter (tubal, uterine, ureteric, vaginal branches). Uterine venous plexus drains into the internal iliac vein. Lymph: fundus and upper body to para-aortic nodes along the ovarian vessels; cornua to superficial inguinal nodes along the round ligament; lower body and cervix to internal iliac nodes.

chunks.title: Self-test: true/false and MCQ with answers
chunks.summary: True/false: angle of version lies between the body and cervix (False; that is the angle of flexion); pubocervical ligament is called Mackenrodt's ligament (False; the transverse cervical ligament is); uterine artery lies lateral to the cervix (True); fundus of the uterus is drained by the para-aortic lymph nodes (True). MCQ: the structure in the free border of the broad ligament is the uterine tube. Ends with the thank-you slide.

chunks.title: Ovary: site, size, ovarian fossa, surfaces, borders and ends
chunks.summary: Title slide (Prof. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany). Ovary: pelvic organ in the ovarian fossa on the lateral pelvic wall, attached to the broad ligament by the mesovarium; almond-shaped, about 3 cm long x 2 cm wide x 1 cm thick. Ovarian fossa bounded posteriorly by the ureter and internal iliac artery, and laterally by the obturator nerve and vessels. Two surfaces (lateral and medial) and 2 borders (anterior attached to the mesovarium, posterior free); tubal (upper) end and uterine (lower) end.

chunks.title: Ovary: peritoneal covering, ends and ligaments
chunks.summary: Ovary is completely covered by peritoneum except the anterior border attached to the mesovarium. Tubal (upper) end is attached to the fimbria of the uterine tube and the suspensory ligament; uterine (lower) end is attached to the lateral angle of the uterus by the ligament of the ovary, below and behind the opening of the uterine tube. Ligaments of the ovary: suspensory ligament (upper end to lateral pelvic wall, contains ovarian vessels and nerves), ovarian ligament (uterine end to lateral angle of uterus), mesovarium (anterior border to broad ligament).

chunks.title: Ovary: arterial supply, venous and lymphatic drainage
chunks.summary: Arterial supply: ovarian artery, a branch of the abdominal aorta, runs through the suspensory ligament then the mesovarium to reach the ovary; the uterine artery gives a few branches. Venous drainage by the pampiniform venous plexus forming the ovarian vein: the right ovarian vein drains into the inferior vena cava, the left ovarian vein into the left renal vein. Lymph accompanies the ovarian vessels to the para-aortic lymph nodes at the level of L2.
keywords: right ovarian vein inferior vena cava
left ovarian vein left renal vein

chunks.title: Uterine (Fallopian) tubes: function, parts and supply
chunks.summary: Muscular tube with great mobility; lateral end opens into the peritoneal cavity and medial end into the uterus at the cornu. Function: transport of oocytes by peristalsis and ciliary action. Parts: intramural (inside the uterine wall), isthmus (medial, narrowest), ampulla (site of fertilization of the ova), infundibulum (funnel-shaped with finger-like fimbriae that lead the ovum after ovulation to the tube opening). Arterial supply: ovarian and uterine arteries; venous: uterine and ovarian veins; lymph: para-aortic and superficial inguinal nodes.

chunks.title: Vagina: description, relations, fornices, supports, supply, paracentesis
chunks.summary: Vagina: muscular tube joining the reproductive tract with the exterior; 7 to 10 cm long; descends antero-inferiorly from the cervix to the vestibule; orifice partly closed by the hymen. Relations: anteriorly base of the bladder and urethra; posteriorly upper quarter covered by peritoneum of the Douglas pouch, middle half related to the rectum, lower quarter separated from the anal canal by the perineal body. Cervix is inserted into the anterior wall; the vaginal cavity around it is the fornix: 4 fornices (anterior, posterior, 2 lateral). Supports: pelvic floor muscles, ligaments of the cervix, perineal body. Supply: vaginal artery and vaginal branches of the uterine artery; vaginal vein drains to the internal iliac vein; lymph to external iliac, internal iliac and superficial inguinal nodes. Clinical note: fluid, blood or pus in the Douglas pouch can be drained by a needle through the posterior fornix (paracentesis).

chunks.title: Female external genitalia and greater vestibular glands
chunks.summary: External genitalia: 2 lateral folds (labia majora), 2 medial folds (labia minora) and the clitoris. Vestibule of the vagina is the space between the labia minora where the urethra, vagina and ducts of the greater vestibular glands open. Greater vestibular (Bartholin's) glands: pea-shaped mucous glands deep to the labia majora; ducts open in the vestibule lateral to the vaginal orifice; secrete during sexual arousal; infection leads to Bartholin abscess.

chunks.title: Self-test: true/false and MCQ with answers
chunks.summary: True/false: ovary is attached to the broad ligament by the mesovarium (True); left ovarian vein drains into the inferior vena cava (False; into the left renal vein); infundibulum of the uterine tube is the site of fertilization (False; the ampulla is); greater vestibular glands lie deep to the labia majora (True). MCQ: the posterior border of the ovarian fossa is formed by the ureter. Ends with the thank-you slide.

chunks.title: Breast: ILOs, definition and shape
chunks.summary: Title slide (Lect. 19: The Female Mammary Gland, Prof. Dr. Maha Diaa Safwat) and learning objectives: relate structure to clinical application, illustrate blood supply, appraise the clinical importance of lymphatic drainage, describe developmental stages and abnormalities. Definition: a modified sweat gland concerned with milk secretion; glandular tissue embedded in the superficial fascia of the pectoral region. Shape: hemispherical with an axillary tail extending from the upper lateral part into the axilla; size, shape and contour vary with age, body weight and lactation; in males the glandular tissue is rudimentary with scanty fat.

chunks.title: Breast: base, retromammary space and structure
chunks.summary: Base rests on pectoralis major, serratus anterior and external oblique; extends from the 2nd to the 6th ribs and from the sternal margin to the midaxillary line. The nipple lies opposite the 5th intercostal space in males and in females before puberty. The retromammary space (loose areolar tissue) separates the breast from the muscles and allows some movement. Structure: glandular tissue divided into lobules by fibrous septa called suspensory ligaments (deep fascia to skin, support the breast); a lactiferous duct arises from each lobule and runs radially to open on the nipple; fatty tissue; nipple; areola (pigmented skin around the nipple).

chunks.title: Breast: arterial supply, venous and lymphatic drainage
chunks.summary: Arterial supply: perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery, anterior intercostal arteries, and lateral thoracic and thoraco-acromial branches of the axillary artery. Veins accompany the arteries. Lymphatics: superficial lymphatics drain the skin and form the subareolar lymphatic plexus; deep lymphatics: lateral quadrants drain to the anterior axillary (pectoral) nodes, medial quadrants along the internal thoracic artery to the parasternal nodes; some vessels communicate with the opposite breast and the anterior abdominal wall; the axillary tail drains to the subscapular group of axillary nodes.

chunks.title: Breast clinical notes: cancer signs, abscess, gynecomastia
chunks.summary: Breast cancer diagnostic signs: dimpling of the skin (invasion and shortening of the suspensory ligaments); inversion/retraction of the nipple (invasion and shortening of the lactiferous ducts); peau d'orange (blocked lymphatics, so the skin becomes thick, oedematous and pitted like orange skin); fixation of the breast (invasion of underlying structures). Breast abscess should be incised radially to minimize injury to the lactiferous ducts. Gynecomastia is enlargement of the male breast.

chunks.title: Development of the mammary glands
chunks.summary: Milk ridge: ectodermal thickening on each side from the axilla to the inguinal region. In humans it disappears except in the pectoral region where a thickened depressed area persists and sends 15-20 buds into the underlying mesoderm; canalization of the buds forms lactiferous ducts, whose branches form smaller ducts and alveoli; ducts open in the depressed area, the future nipple. The area around the nipple darkens to form the areola. In neonates the nipple is depressed and becomes elevated soon after birth through proliferation of underlying mesoderm. Fat develops from mesoderm. Development is the same in both sexes; in females the duct system and fat deposition are due to female sex hormones.

chunks.title: Congenital abnormalities of the breast
chunks.summary: Polymastia: extra mammary glands due to persistence of the milk ridge. Macromastia: abnormally large mammary glands. Micromastia: abnormally small glands. Polythelia: multiple nipples along the milk ridge. Retracted nipple: incomplete development with difficulty in suckling. Gynecomastia: unilateral or bilateral enlargement of the male breasts due to hormonal imbalance.

chunks.title: Self-test: true/false and MCQs; references
chunks.summary: True/false (answers on slide): base of mammary gland extends from 2nd to 6th ribs (True); peau d'orange is due to invasion of lactiferous ducts (False, it is due to lymphatic blockage); milk ridge extends from the axilla to the inguinal region (True); breast abscess is incised transversely (False, radially). MCQs without printed answers: which artery does not supply the breast (options include internal mammary, lateral thoracic, suprascapular, intercostal) and the main lymphatic drainage of the lateral quadrants (subscapular, pectoral axillary, parasternal, lateral axillary). References: Gray's Anatomy, Snell's Clinical Anatomy, Netter Atlas.

chunks.title: Testis: site, functions and coverings
chunks.summary: Title slide (Prof. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany). Testis lies in the scrotum, where the temperature is lower than body temperature because spermatogenesis needs a lower temperature. Functions: production of sperms and of testosterone. Covered by the tunica albuginea, thickened posteriorly to form the mediastinum; the rete testis (canals in the mediastinum) connects to the epididymis by efferent ductules. The testis invaginates the tunica vaginalis sac, so it is covered by an inner visceral layer and an outer parietal layer.

chunks.title: Testis supply and varicocele
chunks.summary: Arterial supply: testicular artery from the abdominal aorta. Venous drainage: pampiniform plexus forming the testicular vein; the right vein drains into the IVC, the left vein into the left renal vein. Lymph: para-aortic nodes. Nerve supply: sympathetic (T10). Clinical note, varicocele: enlarged dilated tortuous veins of the pampiniform plexus; more common on the left because the left testicular vein enters the left renal vein at a right angle, impeding venous return, whereas the right enters the IVC at an acute angle; feels like a bag of worms in the scrotum; treated surgically.
keywords: left testicular vein left renal vein

chunks.title: Scrotum and epididymis
chunks.summary: Scrotum: sac containing the 2 testes, divided by a septum into 2 compartments; has thin dark skin, dartos muscle (replaces the fatty layer of superficial fascia; contracts to give the wrinkled appearance) and the membranous layer (Colles' fascia). Epididymis: convoluted tubule above and behind the testis; functions: maturation and storage of sperms; head, body and tail; head connected to the testis by efferent ductules; tail continuous with the vas deferens; separated from the testis laterally by the sinus; blood supply testicular artery and vein.

chunks.title: Vas deferens, seminal vesicles and ejaculatory ducts
chunks.summary: Vas deferens (ductus deferens): continuation of the epididymis; passes in the spermatic cord through the inguinal canal into the abdomen then the pelvis; on the base of the bladder it lies medial to the seminal vesicle and dilates to form the ampulla; transports sperms from the epididymis to the ejaculatory duct; artery to vas deferens from the inferior vesical artery. Seminal vesicles: 2, on the base of the bladder lateral to the ampulla of the vas; secrete the major part (60%) of seminal fluid; supplied by inferior vesical and middle rectal arteries. Ejaculatory ducts: 2, each formed by the union of the vas deferens and seminal vesicle behind the bladder neck; pierce the prostate to open in the prostatic urethra.

chunks.title: Prostate: site, shape and relations
chunks.summary: Prostate lies below the urinary bladder around the upper part of the urethra; triangular with the base upwards near the bladder neck and the apex downwards on the pelvic floor; has 2 lateral surfaces. The urethra (prostatic urethra) passes through it and the 2 ejaculatory ducts pierce it to open into the prostatic urethra. Secretes about 30% of the seminal fluid. Relations: anteriorly fat in the retropubic space; posteriorly the rectum; laterally the levator ani (pelvic floor). Prostatic ducts open into the prostatic urethra.

chunks.title: Prostate: lobes, coverings, supply and hypertrophy
chunks.summary: Lobes: anterior (anterior to the prostatic urethra, fibromuscular, no glandular tissue); median (above the 2 ejaculatory ducts, behind the urethra, the most glandular part); posterior (below the ejaculatory ducts); right and left lobes. Coverings: inner true capsule and outer fibrous false capsule. Arterial supply: inferior vesical and middle rectal arteries. Venous drainage: prostatic venous plexus between the 2 capsules, draining into the internal iliac veins and communicating with the vesical and vertebral venous plexuses. Lymph: internal iliac nodes. Clinical note, benign prostatic hypertrophy: the median lobe may enlarge in old age, pressing on the urethra with difficulty in micturition and elevating the uvula of the bladder so urine accumulates behind it with recurrent infections.

chunks.title: Bulbourethral glands and penis (root, body, glans)
chunks.summary: Bulbourethral glands: 2, on either side of the membranous urethra in the deep perineal pouch; mucoid secretion; ducts pierce the perineal membrane to open in the penile urethra. Penis: root, body and glans. Root: enlarged bulb (pierced by the urethra) and 2 crura along the pubic arch. Body: 3 cylindrical masses; the corpus spongiosum lies ventrally, continuous with the bulb, contains the urethra and expands distally as the glans; the 2 corpora cavernosa lie dorsally, each continuous with a crus. Glans penis is the expanded end of the corpus spongiosum; the prepuce is a mucocutaneous fold covering the glans, removed by circumcision.

chunks.title: Blood supply of the penis
chunks.summary: Arteries (branches of the internal pudendal artery): dorsal arteries (2, on the dorsum), deep arteries (2, in the corpus cavernosum) and arteries of the bulb (2, in the corpus spongiosum). Veins: superficial dorsal vein drains into the great saphenous vein; deep dorsal vein drains into the prostatic venous plexus. Lymphatic drainage: superficial inguinal lymph nodes.

chunks.title: Self-test: true/false and MCQ with answers
chunks.summary: True/false: vas deferens lies lateral to the seminal vesicle on the bladder base (False, it lies medial); left testicular vein drains into the IVC (False, into the left renal vein); posterior lobe of the prostate lies above the ejaculatory ducts (False, below); corpus spongiosum is connected to the bulb of the penis (True). MCQ: the most glandular prostatic lobe is the median lobe. Ends with the thank-you slide.
keywords: vas deferens medial to seminal vesicle

chunks.title: Perineum: ILOs, definition, boundaries and triangles
chunks.summary: Title slide and ILOs: identify boundaries and divisions of the perineum, describe its fascial layers, boundaries and contents of the superficial and deep perineal pouches, locate the perineal membrane and structures piercing it. Perineum: lowermost part of the trunk including the structures that occupy the pelvic outlet. Diamond-shaped area bounded anteriorly by the lower border of the symphysis pubis, laterally by the pubic arch, ischial tuberosities and sacrotuberous ligaments, posteriorly by the tip of the coccyx. A transverse line joining the anterior ends of the ischial tuberosities divides it into the anal triangle and the urogenital triangle.

chunks.title: Urogenital triangle: boundaries and contents
chunks.summary: Boundaries of the urogenital triangle: anteriorly the lower border of the symphysis pubis; laterally the pubic arch; posteriorly an imaginary line between the ischial tuberosities. Contents: urethra, external genital organs, and the fascial pouches (superficial and deep perineal pouches). Introduces the fascia of the urogenital triangle.

chunks.title: Fascial layers of the urogenital triangle
chunks.summary: Layers from superficial to deep: 1) skin and adipose layer; 2) membranous layer of superficial fascia, Colles' fascia in the perineum (continuous with Scarpa's fascia of the anterior abdominal wall); 3) superficial perineal pouch; 4) perineal membrane (inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm); 5) deep pouch (urogenital diaphragm); 6) superior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm.

chunks.title: Superficial perineal pouch: boundaries and contents (male and female)
chunks.summary: Boundaries: superior the perineal membrane; inferior Colles' fascia; lateral the pubic arch; posteriorly closed by fusion of Colles' fascia and the perineal membrane; anteriorly open and continuous with the space deep to the membranous fascia of the anterior abdominal wall. Male contents: root of the penis (bulb and crura); 3 pairs of muscles (superficial transverse perineal, ischiocavernosus covering the crura, bulbospongiosus covering the bulb); deep and dorsal arteries of the penis and scrotal arteries; dorsal nerve of the penis and scrotal nerves; deep dorsal vein of the penis. Female contents: root of the clitoris (2 bulbs of the vestibule and 2 crura); the same 3 pairs of muscles; deep and dorsal arteries of the clitoris and labial arteries; dorsal nerve of the clitoris and labial nerves; deep dorsal vein of the clitoris; greater vestibular glands deep to the bulb on each side, ducts opening in the vestibule lateral to the vaginal opening.

chunks.title: Deep perineal pouch: boundaries and contents (male and female)
chunks.summary: Deep perineal pouch (urogenital diaphragm) is a completely closed space. Boundaries: superior the superior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm; inferior the perineal membrane; laterally, roof and floor fused with the pubic arch; posteriorly and anteriorly closed by fusion of roof and floor. Male contents: membranous urethra; bulbourethral glands; deep transverse perineal muscle and sphincter urethrae; internal pudendal arteries and arteries of the bulb; dorsal nerve of the penis. Female contents: urethra; vagina; deep transverse perineal muscle and sphincter urethrae around the urethra and vagina; internal pudendal arteries and arteries of the bulb; dorsal nerve of the clitoris.

chunks.title: Perineal membrane and structures piercing it
chunks.summary: Perineal membrane (inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm): fibrous sheet between the superficial and deep perineal pouches, attached laterally to the pubic arch; anterior border thickened as the transverse perineal ligament, separated from the lower border of the symphysis pubis by a space that transmits the deep dorsal vein of the penis or clitoris; posterior border attached to the superior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm and Colles' fascia. Piercing it in males: urethra, ducts of the bulbourethral glands, internal pudendal arteries, arteries of the bulb, dorsal nerves of the penis. In females: urethra, vagina, internal pudendal arteries, arteries of the bulb, dorsal nerves of the clitoris.

chunks.title: Self-test: true/false with answers
chunks.summary: True/false: superficial perineal pouch is attached to Colles' fascia anteriorly (False, it is open anteriorly); deep perineal pouch contains the bulbourethral gland in females (False, it is a male structure); internal pudendal artery pierces the perineal membrane (True); greater vestibular gland is a content of the superficial pouch (True). Ends with the thank-you slide.
keywords: internal pudendal artery pierces perineal membrane

chunks.title: Perineum II: ILOs and recto-anal triangle
chunks.summary: Title slide (Prof. Wafaa Abdel Rahman) and ILOs: identify boundaries and contents of the recto-anal triangle, illustrate the internal pudendal vessels and distribution, identify the pudendal nerve and distribution, appraise the clinical importance of the perineal body. Perineum recap: lowermost part of the trunk (pelvic outlet), divided by a transverse line between the ischial tuberosities into anal and urogenital triangles. Recto-anal triangle boundaries: anteriorly an imaginary line between the ischial tuberosities, laterally the sacrotuberous ligaments, posteriorly the tip of the coccyx. Contents: lower part of the anal canal and an ischiorectal fossa on each side.

chunks.title: Ischiorectal fossa: boundaries and contents
chunks.summary: Wedge-shaped space on each side of the anal canal. Boundaries: anteriorly the posterior border of the perineal membrane and the superficial and deep transverse perineal muscles; posteriorly the sacrotuberous ligament; laterally the obturator internus muscle and fascia and the pudendal canal; medially a sloping wall made by levator ani and the external anal sphincter; superiorly the tendinous line of the obturator fascia (origin of levator ani); inferiorly the skin of the perineum. Contents: ischiorectal pad of fat (allows distension of the anal canal during defecation); inferior rectal and scrotal or labial vessels; inferior rectal and scrotal or labial nerves.

chunks.title: The pudendal canal
chunks.summary: The pudendal canal (Alcock's canal) is a splitting of the obturator fascia on the medial side of the ischial tuberosity, forming the lateral wall of the ischiorectal fossa. Contents: internal pudendal artery and pudendal nerve. Diagram pages relate it to the lesser sciatic foramen and the deep perineal pouch.

chunks.title: Pudendal nerve: origin, course, termination and branches
chunks.summary: Origin: one of the two terminal branches of the sacral plexus. Course: leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen to the gluteal region, then through the lesser sciatic foramen to the perineum, passing through the pudendal canal. Termination: perineal nerve and dorsal nerve of the penis or clitoris. Branches: 1) inferior rectal nerve (passes in the ischiorectal fossa to supply the external anal sphincter and levator ani); 2) perineal nerve (muscular branches to the perineal muscles; scrotal or labial nerves to the scrotum or labia majora); 3) dorsal nerve of the penis or clitoris (pierces the perineal membrane and supplies the dorsal aspect of the penis or clitoris).

chunks.title: Internal pudendal artery: origin, course and branches
chunks.summary: Origin: one of the two terminal branches of the anterior division of the internal iliac artery. Course: leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen to the gluteal region, then through the lesser sciatic foramen to the perineum; passes through the pudendal canal, then through the deep perineal pouch and pierces the perineal membrane. Branches (diagram): inferior rectal artery, perineal artery, artery of the bulb. Termination: division into 2 terminal branches, the dorsal artery and the deep artery of the penis or clitoris.

chunks.title: Perineal body and clinical note
chunks.summary: Perineal body: a fibro-muscular mass attached to the posterior border of the perineal membrane, lying between the openings of the vagina and anal canal. It gives attachment to levator ani, the external anal sphincter, the muscles of the superficial perineal pouch (superficial transverse perineal and bulbospongiosus) and of the deep perineal pouch (deep transverse perineal and urethral sphincter). Clinical note: the perineal body may be injured during labour with prolapse of the pelvic organs.

chunks.title: Kidney and ureter: ILOs, urinary system, kidney site, size and shape
chunks.summary: Title slide (Lect. 39: kidney and ureter, Anat. 12) and ILOs: describe site, size, shape and position of kidney and ureter; relate their location to surrounding organs; correlate blood supply and innervation with origin; correlate ureteric innervation with renal pain and ureteric stones. Urinary system: 2 kidneys, 2 ureters, urinary bladder, urethra. Kidneys lie on the posterior abdominal wall on either side of the vertebral column, extending T12 to L3; the right kidney lies slightly lower than the left because of the large right lobe of the liver. Size about 12 cm x 6 cm x 4 cm. Shape: 2 borders (medial, lateral), 2 poles (superior, inferior), 2 surfaces (anterior, posterior).

chunks.title: Coverings of the kidney
chunks.summary: From inside out: fibrous capsule (closely applied to the kidney surface); perinephric (perirenal) fat covering the capsule; renal fascia, a condensation of connective tissue outside the perinephric fat that encloses the kidneys and suprarenal glands; paranephric (pararenal) fat external to the renal fascia, which supports the kidneys and holds them in position on the posterior abdominal wall.

chunks.title: Internal structure of the kidney
chunks.summary: The kidney is made of an outer cortex and an inner medulla. Cortex: outer region that sends renal columns between the pyramids of the medulla. Medulla: inner part made of renal pyramids that open into the minor calyces; the minor calyces open into major calyces, which join to form the renal pelvis, the upper part of the ureter.

chunks.title: Hilum of the kidney and its contents
chunks.summary: The renal hilum lies at the level of the transpyloric plane (L1) on the medial concave border of each kidney. Structures in the hilum from anterior to posterior: renal vein (most anterior), renal artery (middle), pelvis of the ureter (most posterior), remembered as VAP.

chunks.title: Surfaces and anterior relations of the kidney (diagrams)
chunks.summary: Headings and diagram pages for the surfaces of the kidney and the anterior relations of the right and left kidneys (see the text page that follows for the list of organs).

chunks.title: Anterior relations of the kidneys
chunks.summary: Diagrams and list. Right kidney anteriorly: suprarenal gland, liver, second part of the duodenum, right colic flexure, coils of small intestine. Left kidney anteriorly: suprarenal gland, spleen, stomach, pancreas, left colic flexure, coils of small intestine.

chunks.title: Posterior relations of the kidneys
chunks.summary: Right kidney posteriorly: diaphragm; 12th rib; psoas, quadratus lumborum and transversus abdominis muscles; the subcostal (T12), iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves lie between the kidney and the muscles. Left kidney posteriorly: diaphragm; 11th and 12th ribs; the same muscles and nerves. The left kidney is related to the 11th and 12th ribs, the right to the 12th rib only.

chunks.title: Kidney: blood supply, segments, venous and lymphatic drainage
chunks.summary: Renal arteries arise from the abdominal aorta at L2. Near the hilum each artery divides into five segmental end arteries supplying the kidney segments: apical, anterior superior, anterior inferior, lower (inferior) and posterior. Renal vein runs anterior to the renal artery as it leaves the hilum and drains into the inferior vena cava. Lymphatic drainage: para-aortic and lumbar lymph nodes.

chunks.title: Ureter: abdominal, pelvic and intramural parts
chunks.summary: Three parts: abdominal, pelvic, intramural. Abdominal part: the renal pelvis is the funnel-shaped upper end of the ureter within the hilum; the ureter runs vertically downward behind the peritoneum on psoas major, which separates it from the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae. Pelvic part: enters the pelvis by crossing the bifurcation of the common iliac artery, runs down the lateral pelvic wall to the level of the ischial spine, then turns forward to enter the lateral angle of the bladder. Intramural part: runs obliquely through the bladder wall; this oblique course makes the opening act like a valve preventing backflow of urine.

chunks.title: Ureteric constrictions and relations of the ureter
chunks.summary: Sites of ureteric constriction: pelvi-ureteric junction, the pelvic brim, and the intramural part of the ureter. Anterior relations: right ureter, duodenum, small intestine and right testicular or ovarian arteries; left ureter, small intestine, sigmoid colon and left testicular or ovarian arteries. Posterior relations: psoas major muscle and the genitofemoral nerve.

chunks.title: Ureter: arterial supply, venous and lymphatic drainage
chunks.summary: Arterial supply by part: renal pelvis from the renal artery; abdominal part from the aorta and testicular/ovarian arteries; pelvic part from testicular/ovarian and internal iliac arteries; intravesical part from the inferior vesical artery. Veins correspond to the arteries. Lymphatic drainage: internal and external iliac lymph nodes.

chunks.title: Applied anatomy: ureteric stones, renal pain and colic
chunks.summary: Ureteric stones (calculi) commonly develop at the narrow sites; a calculus in the pelvic part of the ureter causes referred pain to the testis and tip of the penis in males and to the labium majus in females. Renal pain is referred to the flank and may radiate downward into the lower abdomen. In renal colic the renal pelvis and ureter send afferent nerves to spinal cord segments T11, T12, L1 and L2; spasm of smooth muscle causes agonizing colicky pain referred to the skin areas of those segments: flank, loin and groin.

chunks.title: Self-test MCQs and references
chunks.summary: MCQs without printed answers: which structure is not related to the anterior surface of the right kidney (options ascending colon, right lobe of liver, second part of duodenum, coils of small intestine), and which structure does not cross the left ureter anteriorly (small intestine, sigmoid colon, duodenum, gonadal vessels). Per the lecture's relations lists, the right kidney's colic relation is the right colic flexure and the duodenum is not an anterior relation of the left ureter. References: Gray's Anatomy, Snell's Clinical Anatomy, Netter Atlas.
